checks.method: Read CompletionCompatibility.lean and compare its equality, nonempty intersection, and distinctness branches with Section 4.2; explicitly inspect all possible intersection sizes of two two-element coordinate edges.
checks.observation: Equal coordinate edges are treated separately from singleton intersections. Distinct residual completions are required for the sunflower contradiction; x is absent from both, so the constructed star member is distinct. If both coordinates are disjoint, R is disjoint from both completions, giving three distinct petals. Coordinate images jointly determine a completion, justifying the product bound.
checks.scope: Exhaustiveness and distinctness in the split-pair geometry

checks.method: Read TwoStarResidual.lean and GenericHeavyExtensions.lean; check hypotheses on ambient type, noncooccurrence, key nonemptiness and the insertion map.
checks.observation: The trace lemma permits arbitrary Type* and derives y outside U from noncooccurrence. It uses the transversal lower bound rather than a coordinate census. The general key bound has an explicit empty-K branch; in the application n2>=24 supplies nonemptiness. Extension points lie outside keys, so erasing the common extension point proves injection.
checks.scope: Rival explanations based on hidden support restrictions or empty cases

checks.method: Exhaustively enumerate all subfamilies of a five-cycle edge set and all simple graphs on four vertices; enumerate all 8008 six-point nonnegative integer weight vectors with total at most ten and intersect all pairs carrying at least nine units.
checks.observation: Largest pairwise-intersecting five-cycle edge family has size 2; largest four-vertex graph with maximum degree 2 has 4 edges. No heavy-pair common-point counterexample occurs in the 8008 weight vectors. These finite tests corroborate local steps only; the arbitrary-family claim rests on the structural proofs.
checks.scope: Bounded counterexample tests for local combinatorial caps

findings.disposition: No missing geometric case was found in Section 4.2 or the corresponding CompletionCompatibility source.
findings.statement: The split-completion contradiction covers all intersection cardinalities 0, 1 and 2 of two coordinate edges. The 0 case uses R; the positive cases use an x-star member, which is automatically distinct from residual members because it contains x.

findings.disposition: The claimed method boundary is supported by the inspected theorem interfaces and case analyses.
findings.statement: The support-trace and heavy-key arguments are quantified over arbitrary finite families and derive restrictions from sunflower-freeness, not a presumed 17-point or 28-position normalization. The 17-point profile is used only where actual Profile A supplies it.

content.summary: The geometric case analysis is exhaustive for actual set families, including equal or singleton-intersecting coordinate edges, distinctness of sunflower petals, empty residual families, arbitrary ambient support, and empty key collections. No finite-search normalization or numerical-profile surrogate is needed in these steps. Targeted counterexample checks agree with the structural bounds but are not substituted for the proofs.
